**GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:**  
The CalAIM Housing Navigator is responsible for providing Housing Navigation, Housing Deposit, and Housing Tenancy and Sustaining Services to eligible Medi\-Cal participants experiencing homelessness, housing instability, or at risk of losing housing. The Housing Navigator works collaboratively with clients, landlords, property managers, community partners, healthcare providers, and social service agencies to identify and secure safe, stable housing while supporting participants in maintaining long term housing stability. This position requires strong case management, advocacy, resource coordination, and documentation skills to ensure compliance with CalAIM Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and Community Supports requirements, contractual obligations, and organizational policies. **ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Conduct housing related assessments and develop individualized housing plans that identify participant needs, barriers, strengths, and goals while coordinating services that support successful housing placement and stability.
* Assist participants in locating, applying for, and securing safe and affordable housing by providing housing navigation, advocacy, landlord engagement, application support, and linkage to community housing resources.
* Coordinate and facilitate Housing Deposit services, including eligibility determination, documentation, and payment of approved housing related expenses such as security deposits, utility deposits, application fees, and essential move in needs.
* Provide Housing Tenancy and Sustaining Services by educating participants on tenant rights and responsibilities, promoting independent living skills, supporting access to community resources, and implementing interventions that prevent housing loss and promote long term stability.
* Collaborate with healthcare providers, managed care plans, community partners, landlords, and other service agencies to ensure comprehensive care coordination and successful participant outcomes.
* Maintain accurate and timely documentation of assessments, service plans, participant contacts, referrals, housing outcomes, and other required activities in accordance with CalAIM, Medi\-Cal, and organizational requirements.
* Monitor participant progress, evaluate housing stability outcomes, conduct follow up visits and outreach activities, and adjust service plans as necessary to meet participant needs and program objectives.
* Participate in team meetings, trainings, quality improvement activities, and community engagement efforts while ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, county, health plan, and organizational policies and procedures.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

* High School Diploma or equivalent.
* Experience working in case management or a related field, preferably with a background in healthcare or social services.

**Other Requirements**

* Valid driver’s license and proof of current auto insurance.
* Reliable vehicle with appropriate registration and inspection for travel to client locations and other work\-relatedduties.
* Bilingual, bi\-literate, English/Spanish, English/Punjabi, English/Hmong, and/or other language ability based onprogram needs preferred.
* State regulations require a physical examination, current tuberculosis test, and verified fingerprint andcriminal records clearance before beginning work.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:**

* Ability to read and comprehend documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions andprocedure manuals.
* Ability to respond effectively to sensitive inquiries or complaints
* Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
* Ability to speak effectively before groups of clients or employees of organization.
* Ability to add, subtracts, multiply and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, commonfractions and decimals. Ability to compare rate, ratio and percent.
* Ability to understand and use a variety of computer applications and appropriate software, includingspreadsheets, word processing; and workplace electronic technology, including internet access and email.
* Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral or diagramform.
* Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized or not standardized situation.
* Knowledge of and sensitivity to diversity and understanding the needs of clients from differentcultures and socioeconomic backgrounds.

starting at birth, providing children with monthly books up to age 5, and helping foster

youth with savings accounts as they transition to adulthood. Recognizing that children's

needs extend beyond the classroom, we address immediate basic needs as well like

hunger and housing. This is why we provide housing supportive services, including

catering to 7,000 children.

2023 Sacramento Black Chamber of Commerce Non\-Profit of the Year, the 2023

Sacramento Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce Centennial Business Hall of Fame

Business Journal. These honors reflect our ongoing efforts and commitment to the

United Way’s core is the philosophy that families possess the blueprint for their prosperity.

inclusive approach, spanning from our staff to our initiatives, epitomizes our commitment

to ensure every family, and thereby every community, thrives.

**STATEMENT OF PURPOSE****:**


The primary purpose of the Housing Navigator is to assist families in achieving transitional housing and access medical, educational, social, prevocational, rehabilitative, employment or other needed community services for eligible clients and families who have become homeless. Targeted population includes children (Birth to age 18\) and their families who are at risk of becoming homeless or are currently homeless utilizing a Community Based Scattered Site Model. The Community Based Scattered Site Model is designed to maximize family independence, minimize family disruption, and result in stronger, more viable housing permanency outcomes.

* Monday\-Friday, 8am\-5pm Schedule.
* Hybrid schedule after 90 days.
* Full benefits package to all positions after 30 days of employment.
* Free standard HMO Health, Dental, and Vision plans offered to employees.

5Cities Homeless Coalition assists those who are experiencing or at\-risk of homelessness to achieve housing stability, self\-sufficiency, and improved health by providing resources, supportive services, and programs.
  
  

Our Vision
  
  

Through collaboration and leadership, the Coalition is building an engaged community that fully understands the complexities of homelessness and actively shares the responsibility of creating and implementing solutions to reduce it.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

The Jail to Community Post\-Release Case Manager provides support to individuals experiencing homelessness, focusing on creating housing stability plans, securing permanent housing and connecting clients to community resources. The primary focus is to work in coordination with partner agencies to address a broad array of client needs through referrals to providers of necessary services, and in providing housing assistance. The Case Manager will typically work out of offices in Grover Beach. The Case Manager may perform duties that include coordinated entry, outreach, prevention and risk reduction, crisis intervention, transportation, health education, referral for substance abuse and mental health counseling, and benefits counseling. The Case Manager works with program staff to ensure program funds are used according to grant requirements and maintains quality assurance of client files. Routine duties include interacting with law enforcement, government agencies, faith\-based organizations, local businesses and nonprofit agencies to provide client services.
  
  

Responsibilities
  
  

The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons.
  
  

Program Implementation
  
  

* Manage caseload of 35\-40 participants with varying levels of need.
* Assist clients with obtaining resources, developing case plans, and completing applications for supportive and subsidized housing paperwork.
* Make appropriate referrals for benefits advocacy or help complete benefits applications as appropriate.
* Advocate for clients with agencies and service providers to minimize barriers to clients receiving needed services.
* Connect clients with the appropriate level of care for physical and behavioral health needs.
* Assist clients by managing use of services and expediting service delivery through linkage activities.
* Adhere to CalAIM standards for engaging in Enhanced Care Management and Community Supports Programs.


Case Management
  
  

* Utilizing a housing\-focused approach, create housing stability plans for clients with 30, 60, and 90\-day goals including the steps to achieve those goals.
* Assist clients in job search and employment retention.
* Assist clients in developing savings and budget plans.
* Assist clients with necessary enrollment paperwork for eligible clients to assess health and medical benefits.
* Prepare case\-related reports including outcomes, successes and challenges.
* Complete HMIS data entry related to all client services provided.
* Complete appropriate referrals and maintain adequate supporting documentation for enrollment in CalAIM services including but not limited to Enhanced Care Management, Housing Transition Navigation Services, Housing Tenancy and Sustaining Services, Housing Deposits, Day Habilitation, and Short\-Term Post Hospitalization.
* Engage in best practices of case management while still maintaining adaptability and flexibility.
* Provide relevant referrals to agencies and service providers based upon the goals and objectives mutually agreed upon with clients.


Outreach and Relationship Management
  
  

* Work with supervisor and colleagues on outreach to realtors, landlords, home owners and other housing providers to identify new and existing housing opportunities and build a strong inventory of available housing options for clients.
* Establish and maintain collaborative working relationships with community resources, law enforcement, health agencies, and educational settings.
* Maintain a strong working relationship with partner agencies and sober living environments (SLEs) and Residential Treatment Programs.
* Actively participate in staff meetings and trainings.


Qualifications
  
  

* Possess a minimum of an Associate Degree in a related field or two years of related Case Management experience.
* Experience in non\-profit management, case management and/or program development.
* Background in or familiarity with behavioral health preferred.
* Previous experience with social services and/or homeless programs.
* Able to use computers, with proficiency in Microsoft Office software, particularly Excel.
* Be a highly motivated self\-starter, with proven ability to develop creative solutions.
* Project a professional demeanor and possess excellent written and oral communication skills, interpersonal skills, and ability to work both individually and as part of a team.
* Maintain regular attendance.
* Able to multi\-task and remain calm in demanding and unpredictable situations.
* Able to maintain a professional, customer service\-oriented attitude at all times
* Able to meet face\-to\-face in the office and in unsheltered locations with homeless individuals of diverse backgrounds and disabilities, including physical, mental, substance abuse, HIV/AIDS, etc.
* Able to tolerate being outdoors

The primary purpose of the Housing Navigator is to assist families in achieving transitional housing and access medical, educational, social, prevocational, rehabilitative, employment or other needed community services for eligible clients and families who have become homeless.
